hook: A Möbius band is twisted, yet two of them combine into something untwisted. How do you keep the books?
about: K-theory attaches abelian groups to a ring, a space or an algebraic variety by formally adding and subtracting the vector bundles or projective modules that live on it. The group \(K_0\) records these objects up to a stable form of equivalence, the group \(K_1\) records invertible matrices up to elementary operations, and higher groups continue the pattern.

There are several versions. Topological K-theory is a cohomology theory for spaces, governed by Bott periodicity. Algebraic K-theory of rings and schemes is much harder to compute and carries arithmetic information, such as class groups and special values of zeta functions. Operator K-theory applies to C*-algebras. The subject grew out of the Riemann-Roch theorem and remains tied to index theory, the topology of manifolds and motivic cohomology.

example.title: Two Möbius bands
example.text: Over the circle there are two real line bundles: the trivial one, a cylinder, and the Möbius band \(M\). They are not isomorphic. Yet the direct sum \(M\oplus M\) is isomorphic to the trivial plane bundle over the circle. In K-theory the class \([M]-[1]\) is therefore not zero, but twice it is zero. In fact the reduced real K-group of the circle is \(\mathbb{Z}/2\), generated by this class.

objects.gloss: A family of vector spaces that varies continuously over the points of a space.
A direct summand of a free module; the algebraic counterpart of a vector bundle.
The abelian group obtained from a commutative monoid by adjoining formal differences.
The Grothendieck group of finitely generated projective modules, or of vector bundles, under direct sum.
The group of invertible matrices of all sizes over a ring, made abelian.
Homotopy groups of a space built from the category of projective modules, as defined by Quillen.
A ring homomorphism from K-theory to rational cohomology; for finite complexes an isomorphism after tensoring with the rationals.

theorems.name: Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch theorem
theorems.statement: Let \(f\colon X\to Y\) be a proper morphism of smooth quasi-projective varieties over a field. For every class \(x\) in \(K_0(X)\), \(\mathrm{ch}(f_*x)\,\mathrm{td}(T_Y)=f_*\bigl(\mathrm{ch}(x)\,\mathrm{td}(T_X)\bigr)\) in the rational Chow ring of \(Y\), where \(f_*x\) is defined as the alternating sum of the higher direct images.

theorems.name: Bott periodicity
theorems.statement: For a compact Hausdorff space \(X\), complex K-theory satisfies \(\tilde K(\Sigma^2X)\cong\tilde K(X)\), where \(\Sigma\) denotes reduced suspension. Equivalently, the homotopy groups of the infinite unitary group repeat with period 2. For real K-theory the period is 8.

theorems.name: Hopf invariant one theorem
theorems.statement: For \(n\ge 2\), a continuous map \(S^{2n-1}\to S^n\) of Hopf invariant one exists only when \(n\) is 2, 4 or 8. Adams proved this with cohomology operations; K-theory later gave a short proof.

theorems.name: Serre-Swan theorem
theorems.statement: Let \(X\) be a compact Hausdorff space. Sending a complex vector bundle to its module of continuous sections is an equivalence between the category of vector bundles over \(X\) and the category of finitely generated projective modules over the ring of continuous complex functions on \(X\).

theorems.name: K-theory of finite fields
theorems.statement: For the field \(\mathbb{F}_q\) with \(q\) elements and every \(i\ge 1\), Quillen's K-groups are \(K_{2i}(\mathbb{F}_q)=0\) and \(K_{2i-1}(\mathbb{F}_q)\cong\mathbb{Z}/(q^i-1)\).

theorems.name: Norm residue isomorphism theorem
theorems.statement: Let \(k\) be a field and \(\ell\) a prime different from the characteristic of \(k\). For every \(n\ge 0\), the norm residue map from Milnor K-theory \(K^M_n(k)/\ell\) to the Galois cohomology group \(H^n(k,\mu_\ell^{\otimes n})\) is an isomorphism.

open.name: Farrell-Jones conjecture
open.gloss: Predicts that the algebraic K-theory of a group ring can be computed from the virtually cyclic subgroups of the group; proved for many classes of groups, open in general.

open.name: Baum-Connes conjecture
open.gloss: Predicts that an assembly map computes the K-theory of the reduced C*-algebra of a group from the proper actions of the group; open in general.

open.name: K-groups of the integers
open.gloss: Whether \(K_{4i}(\mathbb{Z})=0\) for every \(i\ge 1\); this is equivalent to Vandiver's conjecture in number theory.
